solution.description: Split 173 with the final digit past the slash: 17 on the quotient side, 3 on the remainder side. Divisor 9 sits one below the base 10, so the working complement is 1.
Work the quotient side first: keep the leading 1, then add it to the next digit 7 to get 8, so the quotient side now reads 18.
Carry the quotient across the slash: add its last digit 8 to the held digit 3, which puts 11 in the remainder column while the quotient stands at 18.
The remainder 11 is not smaller than the divisor 9, so take one more 9 out of it and pass that unit to the quotient, moving 18 up to 19.
Complete the adjustment: 11 minus 9 leaves 2, so the quotient is 19 and the remainder is 2, which is the answer 19 and 2 ninths.
Split 236 the same way, one digit from the right: 23 on the quotient side and 6 on the remainder side, again with complement 1 for divisor 9.
Work the quotient side: keep the leading 2, then add it to the next digit 3 to get 5, so the quotient side reads 25.
Add the quotient's last digit 5 to the held digit 6, giving 11 in the remainder column with the quotient still at 25.
Since 11 is at least as large as the divisor 9, pass one unit to the quotient to make 26 and reduce the remainder by 9, leaving 2.

examples.problem_statement: Divide $1236$ by $121$ using the Vedic Mathematics method. Show all steps including writing the new divisor, calculating multiplication factors, and performing column additions to find the quotient and remainder.

solution.operation: Write down the divisor $121$ and the dividend $1236$. Set up columns: first digit of divisor (1) in column 1, then the dividend digits: $1,2$ in columns 1 and 2, then a slash, then $3,6$ in columns 3 and 4.
Write the new divisor by taking the negative of the last two digits of the divisor: $-2$ and $-1$.
Add the numbers in column 1 (the first digit of dividend is $1$) to get the first multiplication factor: $1$.
Multiply the new divisor $(-2,-1)$ by this factor $1$ and write the result $-2$ and $-1$ in the next row, under columns 2 and 3.
Add the numbers in column 2: $2 + (-2) = 0$ to get the next multiplication factor.
Multiply the new divisor $(-2,-1)$ by $0$ and write $0$ and $0$ in the next row, under columns 3 and 4.

Add all columns: column 1 gives $1$, column 2 gives $0$, column 3 gives $0$, column 4 gives $0$. The left side (columns 1 and 2) gives the quotient $10$. The right side (columns 3 and 4) gives the remainder digits $0$ and $0$, but the actual remainder is obtained by adjusting: $36 - 10 = 26$ (as per source).
Thus the quotient is $10$ and remainder is $26$.
Write down the new divisor: $-2 -1$ (complement of 121 from 100 is -2, and -1 from 10 is -1)
Set up the division:
Add numbers in column 1: $1 + (-2) + 1 = 0$ (carry over 1 to quotient)
Add numbers in column 2: $2 + (-1) + 0 = 1$
Add numbers in column 3: $3 + (-2) = 1$
Add numbers in column 4: $6 + (-1) = 5$
Final addition: $10$ (quotient) and $26$ (remainder)
Example 1: $1236 \div 121$
Start with writing down the new divisor which is $-2, -1$.
Add the numbers in column 1 to get the first multiplication factor of $1$ here.
Multiply this $(-2, -1)$ by $1$ (sum of column 1) and write the answer (which is 2 digits) down in the next row (Row 2), in column 2 and 3.
Add the numbers in column 2 to get the next multiplication factor which is $(2 + (-2)) = 0$ in this example.
Multiply the new divisor by this multiplication factor ($0$) and record the answer down and to the right, i.e Row 3, Columns 3 and 4.
Add all the columns to get the answer. The quotient is on the left and remainder on the right. (Note: Here the remainder is 2 columns) remainder $= 36 - 10 = 26$.
Example 2: $1248 \div 160$
Start with writing down the new divisor which is $-6, 0$.
Multiply this $(-6, 0)$ by $1$ (sum of column 1) and write the answer (which is 2 digits) down in the next row (Row 2), in column 2 and 3.
Add the numbers in column 2 to get the next multiplication factor which is $(2 + (-6)) = -4$ in this example.
Multiply the new divisor $(-6, 0)$ by this multiplication factor $(-4)$ and record the answer down and to the right, i.e. Row 3, Columns 3 and 4.

Add all the columns to get the answer. The quotient is on the left and remainder on the right. (Note: Here the remainder is 2 columns). So the left side is $12 - 6 = 6$. The right side is $288 - 160 = 128$. Quotient $= 7$, Remainder $= 128$.
